explain.say: In spring, birds burst into song just before sunrise, a chorus that can be deafening. This dawn chorus is mostly males, singing to defend their territory and attract mates.

explain.say: At dawn it is often too dim to hunt insects or seeds well, so singing is a good use of time. Birds also burn energy overnight, so a loud song shows a male is healthy and still holds his patch.

explain.say: Song peaks around sunrise and tails off through the morning, with a smaller burst at dusk. Different species start at different times, and birds with bigger eyes, which see better in dim light, tend to start earlier.

faq.a: Male birds sing mainly to defend a territory, telling rivals to keep out, and to attract and keep a mate. A rich, loud song signals a healthy, experienced male.
asks: Why do birds sing in spring?

faq.a: The dawn chorus is the burst of birdsong that starts before sunrise, especially in spring and early summer when birds are breeding. Many species join in at different times.
asks: Why are birds so loud in the morning?

faq.q: Why do some birds sing earlier than others?
faq.a: Birds with larger eyes, which see better in dim light, tend to start singing earlier. Robins and blackbirds are often among the first, while some smaller birds join later.
asks: Which bird sings first in the morning?
Why do robins sing so early?

faq.a: Some do. Nightingales sing at night, especially unpaired males, and robins near bright streetlights or noisy roads often sing at night when it is quieter.
asks: Why is a bird singing in the dark?

faq.a: Yes. Female song is common, especially in the tropics; one study found females sing in about seven in ten songbird species examined, often in duets with their mates.
asks: Why do some birds sing duets?

facts: Birds with larger eyes tend to begin singing earlier in the dawn chorus (Thomas and colleagues, 2002).
Female song was found in about 71 percent of songbird species surveyed (Odom and colleagues, 2014).
